exclusion_pragmas_note: How many `# pragma: no cover` / `no branch` lines exist under backend/app/. A pragma removes its line from `lines-valid` ENTIRELY, so uncovered code added under one is invisible to the `missed` count above -- proven: a genuinely untested helper moved missed 182 -> 185 and failed the gate, and the same helper with a pragma on its def line measured 182 again and PASSED. So suppressions get the same treatment as uncovered lines: a recorded count that must not increase. Not a ban -- all seven are defensible `except Exception:` on shutdown/defensive paths. Enforced by tests/test_coverage_gate_is_a_baseline_not_a_floor.py, not by the gate script, which sees only the report.
gate: missed must not INCREASE. Not a percentage floor -- see #308 and #321.
how_it_was_measured: The root lines-covered/lines-valid attributes of the backend-coverage artifact from six consecutive successful `main` CI runs (34447917136, 34449722396, 34710928493, 34715324929, 34721501302, 34722073332), every one of them bit-identical at covered=5403 / valid=5585, and reproduced locally on a clean worktree with no backend/.env via `make coverage` at b5a3c1036c44e59575f956224af75aad36c8578f (the SHA this file recorded then; measured_at_sha now names the later #455 measurement below). `lines-valid` drifts as app/ grows (5562 -> 5567 -> 5585 across the runs before those), which is why the gate is the integer count and not the percentage. Lowered 182 -> 179 by #455: declaring the users.email unique index made the concurrent-registration branch in app/api/routes/auth.py register (except IntegrityError, rollback, raise) reachable, and test_register_losing_a_concurrent_race_is_422_not_500 covers those 3 lines -- measured locally via `make coverage` (covered=5422 / valid=5601), and 182 with only that test deselected. First recorded against branch commit c0dfadd, which the squash merge of #485 rewrote, so main's own test_the_repos_real_baseline_is_usable_and_self_consistent failed; re-measured at the squash commit 14c878d on a clean worktree with no backend/.env and got the identical covered=5422 / valid=5601. Lowered 179 -> 173 after ADR-0005 Phase 4B-1 (#505): its new tests covered previously unexercised OAuth/GitHub lines (the GitHub email selection was rewritten and every branch is now tested). Measured via `make coverage` on a clean worktree at the squash commit 35753d3, with no backend/.env: covered=6186 / valid=6359 / missed=173.
why_covered_and_valid_go_stale_and_misse: Only `missed` is compared. `covered` and `valid` are the pair AS MEASURED AT measured_at_sha, kept so a reader can reproduce the number, and they are EXPECTED to drift. Demonstrated on this very branch: merging PR #428 (171 changed lines in app/retrieval/keyword.py, unrelated to coverage) moved the measurement to covered=5416 / valid=5598 -- both up by 13 -- and left missed at 182 exactly. A percentage floor would have moved; the count did not. Do not refresh these two fields on every merge; refresh them only when you deliberately change `missed`.
how_to_change_it: SQUASH-MERGE TRAP: PRs here are squash-merged, which rewrites every branch commit, so a measured_at_sha taken on a PR branch passes the ancestor check on the PR and FAILS it on main the moment it merges (#485 did exactly this). When a PR changes missed, merge it, then in a follow-up re-measure at the squash commit and point measured_at_sha there. Lowering it locks in an improvement and needs no justification. RAISING it means shipping lines no test executes: do it in the same commit as the code, and say in the commit message which lines and why they are not testable here.
